correctness.rationale: Leader existence is exactly intersection of the two marginal maximizing-index sets. Conditional exchangeability makes each maximizing set uniform at fixed size, and coordinate independence makes the two sets independent, giving the hypergeometric formula. The upper bound follows from the expected intersection size; the lower bound follows by bounding the exact disjointness product. The two asymptotic equivalences then follow from bounded convergence and elementary tail bounds. No finite experiment is used to establish an infinite statement.

value.rationale: The motivating literature explicitly asks for a computable criterion for leader behavior and leaves the infinite-support product problem open. The result gives a natural structural reduction valid for arbitrary discrete, continuous, or mixed marginals: all two-dimensional product-law leader behavior is controlled by one-dimensional sample-maximum tie multiplicities. The exact identity recovers known continuous cases and isolates the precise obstruction that any resolution of the infinite-support conjecture must control. This is a motivated structural lemma rather than an arbitrary finite slice or routine numerical recomputation.
